text:
A: Hiya, hello! Can you hear me alright?
B: Yeah, I can hear you. Hiya. Craig.
A: Daniel, nice to meet you. I'm in Newark, so East Midlands. Where are you, sorry?
B: Leigh. Greater Manchester, sort of between Wigan and Manchester.
A: Oh, nice. So, er, I'm a director at a lettings firm, it's my dad's business really, sort of family run. I do the day-to-day, tenants, landlords, chasing plumbers, that kind of thing. What do you do?
B: I'm at a primary school. Cleaner and site assistant. In at six to open up, do the bins, check the boiler, then back at half three to do the classrooms.
A: Six! That's early. I do the gym four mornings and I think that's bad, and I'm not up till half six.
B: Up at quarter past five. Doesn't bother me, to be fair. You get used to it.
A: Yeah, no, fair enough. Do you like it?
B: Yeah. Hours suit, nobody's on my back. I was in a warehouse for years before. Picking. This is better.
A: Mm. I bet you get some jobs at a primary school, though.
B: Had to unblock the girls' toilets again this week. Somebody'd put a full roll down. Every term, that.
A: Oh no. We get that with tenants, honestly, you would not believe what people put down a toilet. Grown adults. I had one last year, wet wipes, the whole stack went, and the landlord wanted the tenant charged, and the tenant were in tears on the phone, and I'm stood in the middle trying to keep everyone happy, you know what I mean.
B: Yeah. Kids have got an excuse, at least.
A: Exactly, yeah! I saw your photo, you've got a rugby fixture list on the fridge. Is that Leigh?
B: Leigh Leopards, yeah. Had a season ticket on and off since I were a lad. I go with our kid, my brother. Played till about thirty, open age, then I did my shoulder and packed in.
A: Oh, nice. I'm more football. Forest. I share a season ticket with my dad, we do alternate home games. I get far too wound up, though. I go dead quiet when we're losing.
B: Rugby's the same. You just sit there.
A: Yeah. And the dog, is that yours, the bed in the corner?
B: Yeah, Bella. Staffy. She's getting on a bit now, she can't do the long walk round the flash anymore. Pennington Flash, it's a big lake by us. I fish there as well.
A: Oh, do you? What do you catch?
B: Bit of everything. Had a decent bream last weekend. Sat there four hours for it, mind. Most people think that's boring, but it's the quiet, you know. Nobody ringing you. That's half of it.
A: That sounds amazing, to be honest. My phone never stops. Tenant rang about a boiler on a Sunday recently. Right in the middle of Sunday dinner.
B: Can't you leave it off?
A: I could, I suppose. I just hate letting anyone down. Do you go away much?
B: Caravan near Abersoch most years. Booked it for August. And somewhere hot every couple of years, Tenerife usually, or Majorca.
A: Tenerife! I've been three times. Same resort with the lads. It's funny, the lady I just spoke to, she's been three times as well.
B: It's easy, to be fair. Pool, a bar, somewhere to watch the rugby. Don't need much else.
A: No, definitely. And a decent breakfast. Do they do a proper bacon cob out there? Sorry, a bacon roll, I mean.
B: A barm. Bacon barm. Not like home, no.
A: A barm, yeah, that's it! Hannah, my girlfriend, she says bap, and we argue about it every single
